worked_solution:
First, we rearrange our equation into a form that is more convenient for logarithms, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{y+1}-1 & =3 \\ {e}^{y+1} & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we find the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation and solve for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{y+1} & =4 \\ ln⁡({e}^{y+1}) & =ln⁡(4) \\ y+1 & =2ln⁡(2) \\ y & =2ln⁡(2)-1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $y=2ln⁡(2)-1.$
